The 1933 cartoon by Clifford Berryman shows the political debate over Franklin Roosevelt's New Deal programs, depicting both supporters and critics of expanded federal intervention in the economy during the Great Depression.

What was the primary economic problem the New Deal was designed to address?

choices.text: Mass unemployment, bank failures, and collapse of industrial and agricultural production
Runaway inflation that made everyday goods unaffordable for most American families
Overproduction in factories causing prices to rise and consumers unable to afford goods
A growing trade deficit with European nations that was draining American gold reserves

items.explanation: A is correct: The Great Depression (1929-1939) was characterized by mass unemployment (reaching 25% by 1933), deflation, bank failures, and a collapse in consumer spending and industrial production. The New Deal's programs were primarily designed to put people back to work, stabilize the banking system, and restore economic confidence. B is incorrect: inflation was not the problem of the Depression era; deflation (falling prices) was the concern. C is incorrect: the Depression was characterized by falling industrial output, not overproduction causing high prices. D is incorrect: the U.S. trade deficit was not the defining problem of the Great Depression.

choices.textEs: La AAA priorizó los intereses de las grandes granjas comerciales sobre los agricultores familiares y los pobres urbanos, reflejando la tendencia del New Deal a favorecer los intereses económicos establecidos sobre los estadounidenses más vulnerables.

choices.text: The AAA was designed primarily to protect large agricultural corporations from bankruptcy, and the decision to destroy crops was a political compromise that allowed the Roosevelt administration to maintain the support of Southern Democrats.
choices.textEs: La AAA fue diseñada principalmente para proteger a las grandes corporaciones agrícolas de la quiebra, y la decisión de destruir cosechas fue un compromiso político que permitió a la administración Roosevelt mantener el apoyo de los demócratas sureños.

items.explanation: The AAA's logic was grounded in supply economics: in a deflationary spiral, falling prices destroy farm income, causing farms to fail, which eliminates food production capacity for the long term. The immediate moral cost (destroying food while people starved) was presented as necessary to stabilize the supply-side of the agricultural economy and prevent a complete collapse of farm income. The controversy is real — it was both economically logical and morally troubling simultaneously. Students must analyze a policy's internal economic rationale while evaluating its moral trade-offs — the hallmark of DOK 3 analytical thinking.
items.explanationEs: La lógica de la AAA se basaba en la economía de la oferta: en una espiral deflacionaria, la caída de los precios destruye los ingresos agrícolas, lo que hace que las granjas quiebren, eliminando la capacidad de producción de alimentos a largo plazo. El costo moral inmediato (destruir alimentos mientras la gente pasaba hambre) se presentó como necesario para estabilizar el lado de la oferta de la economía agrícola y evitar un colapso completo de los ingresos agrícolas.

items.stem: The Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) is often cited as one of the most transformative New Deal programs. A historian argues the TVA's significance went beyond flood control and electricity generation. Which analysis BEST captures the TVA's broader transformative impact?
items.stemEs: La Autoridad del Valle de Tennessee (TVA) se cita a menudo como uno de los programas más transformadores del New Deal. Un historiador argumenta que la importancia de la TVA fue más allá del control de inundaciones y la generación de electricidad. ¿Qué análisis captura MEJOR el impacto transformador más amplio de la TVA?

choices.text: The TVA's most significant impact was employing unemployed Tennessee workers during the Depression, proving that direct federal job creation was more effective than relying on private-sector hiring to restore employment during a severe economic crisis.
choices.textEs: El impacto más significativo de la TVA fue crear empleos para los trabajadores desempleados en Tennessee, lo que demostró que el empleo federal directo era más efectivo que la creación de empleo en el sector privado durante una depresión.

choices.text: The TVA's broader legacy was providing a replicable model for government-led regional development that directly influenced how the United States structured foreign aid and economic development programs in the postwar period.
choices.textEs: La importancia más amplia de la TVA fue que proporcionó un modelo para los programas de desarrollo internacional, influyendo en cómo Estados Unidos abordó la ayuda exterior después de la Segunda Guerra Mundial.

choices.text: The TVA showed the federal government could serve as direct economic planner — providing below-market electricity that challenged private utilities while transforming one of the nation's most impoverished regions — setting a precedent for ongoing debates about government's economic role.
choices.textEs: La TVA demostró que el gobierno federal podía actuar como planificador y desarrollador económico directo, proporcionando electricidad a tarifas por debajo del mercado que desafiaba a los servicios públicos privados mientras transformaba una de las regiones más empobrecidas del país, estableciendo un precedente para debates continuos sobre el papel del gobierno en la economía.

choices.text: The TVA's most enduring long-term impact was environmental: controlling the Tennessee River system eliminated the destructive seasonal flooding that had historically devastated agricultural land and prevented sustainable farming development throughout the region.
choices.textEs: El impacto más significativo a largo plazo de la TVA fue ambiental: al controlar el sistema del río Tennessee, evitó las inundaciones que históricamente habían devastado las tierras agrícolas y permitió el desarrollo de la agricultura sostenible en la región.

items.explanation: The TVA demonstrated that the federal government could act as a direct economic developer — building infrastructure, providing electricity at below-market rates to undermine private utility monopolies, and stimulating regional economic development in one of the most impoverished regions of the country. It was a model of federal planning that generated intense controversy (it was essentially a government-owned utility competing with private enterprise) and became a template for ongoing debates about the proper role of government in economic development. Students must synthesize the TVA's multiple dimensions of impact beyond the most surface-level facts.
items.explanationEs: La TVA demostró que el gobierno federal podía actuar como desarrollador económico directo: construyendo infraestructura, proporcionando electricidad a tarifas por debajo del mercado para socavar los monopolios de servicios públicos privados y estimulando el desarrollo económico regional en una de las regiones más empobrecidas del país. Era un modelo de planificación federal que generó una intensa controversia y se convirtió en una plantilla para debates continuos sobre el papel apropiado del gobierno en el desarrollo económico.

items.stem: The Social Security Act of 1935 created both an old-age pension system and unemployment insurance. Critics argued it did not go far enough; others argued it went too far. Which analysis identifies the MOST significant long-term structural consequence of the Social Security Act?
items.stemEs: La Ley de Seguridad Social de 1935 creó tanto un sistema de pensiones para la vejez como un seguro de desempleo. Los críticos argumentaban que no llegaba suficientemente lejos; otros argumentaban que iba demasiado lejos. ¿Qué análisis identifica la consecuencia estructural a largo plazo MÁS significativa de la Ley de Seguridad Social?

choices.text: The Social Security Act created a reliable stream of payroll tax revenue that allowed the federal government to fund New Deal programs without raising income taxes on the wealthy.
choices.textEs: La Ley de Seguridad Social creó una fuente confiable de ingresos del impuesto sobre la nómina que permitió al gobierno federal financiar los programas del New Deal sin aumentar los impuestos sobre la renta de los ricos.

choices.text: By providing old-age pensions, the Social Security Act encouraged older workers to retire, freeing up jobs for younger unemployed workers and directly reducing the unemployment rate during the Depression.
choices.textEs: Al proporcionar pensiones de vejez, la Ley de Seguridad Social alentó a los trabajadores mayores a jubilarse, liberando empleos para los trabajadores jóvenes desempleados y reduciendo directamente la tasa de desempleo durante la Depresión.

choices.text: The most significant long-term consequence of Social Security was that it was repeatedly challenged in federal courts, establishing important precedents about the constitutional limits of federal spending power.
choices.textEs: La consecuencia a largo plazo más significativa de la Seguridad Social fue que fue repetidamente impugnada en los tribunales federales, estableciendo precedentes importantes sobre los límites constitucionales del poder de gasto federal.

choices.text: The Social Security Act permanently established the principle that the federal government bears responsibility for citizens' economic security in old age and unemployment, fundamentally reshaping the relationship between the individual and the state.
choices.textEs: La Ley de Seguridad Social estableció permanentemente el principio de que el gobierno federal tiene la responsabilidad del bienestar económico de los ciudadanos en la vejez y el desempleo, reformando fundamentalmente la relación entre el individuo y el Estado.

items.explanation: The Social Security Act's most significant long-term structural consequence was the establishment of the principle that the federal government has a permanent obligation to provide a minimum economic safety net for citizens — fundamentally altering the relationship between the individual and the state. This was a constitutional and philosophical revolution: prior to 1935, social welfare was the domain of family, charity, and local government. After 1935, the federal government became the guarantor of a minimum standard of living in old age and unemployment. This permanent structural change is what students at DOK 3 must reason toward — not simply recall what the act created.
items.explanationEs: La consecuencia estructural a largo plazo más significativa de la Ley de Seguridad Social fue el establecimiento del principio de que el gobierno federal tiene una obligación permanente de proporcionar una red de seguridad económica mínima para los ciudadanos, alterando fundamentalmente la relación entre el individuo y el Estado. Antes de 1935, el bienestar social era dominio de la familia, la caridad y el gobierno local. Después de 1935, el gobierno federal se convirtió en el garante de un nivel de vida mínimo.

items.stem: The Works Progress Administration (WPA) employed millions of Americans in public works, but also funded artists, writers, photographers, and theater productions through special programs. Critics called this wasteful. Defenders argued it served an important function beyond job creation. Which argument BEST justifies the WPA's cultural programs on grounds beyond direct economic relief?
items.stemEs: La Administración de Obras Públicas (WPA) empleó a millones de estadounidenses en obras públicas, pero también financió a artistas, escritores, fotógrafos y producciones teatrales a través de programas especiales. Los críticos lo llamaron un desperdicio. Los defensores argumentaban que servía a una función importante más allá de la creación de empleos. ¿Qué argumento justifica MEJOR los programas culturales de la WPA por razones más allá del alivio económico directo?

choices.text: Cultural programs preserved skilled workers' abilities, documented American life during a historic crisis, and sustained national morale and cultural identity at a moment of profound national despair — functions with long-term value beyond job creation.
choices.textEs: Los programas culturales preservaron las habilidades de los trabajadores especializados, documentaron la vida estadounidense durante una crisis histórica y sostuvieron la moral nacional y la identidad cultural en un momento de profunda desesperación nacional, funciones con valor a largo plazo más allá de la creación de empleos.

choices.text: Cultural programs were justified because skilled artists could not reasonably be employed in construction or physical labor, so special cultural programs were the only practical way to provide relief to this segment of the unemployed.
choices.textEs: Los programas culturales se justificaban porque los artistas especializados no podían ser empleados razonablemente en construcción o trabajo físico, por lo que los programas culturales especiales eran la única forma práctica de proporcionar ayuda a este segmento de los desempleados.

choices.text: Cultural programs were justified because American art and literature exported by the WPA served as soft power tools that enhanced American prestige abroad during a period of rising fascism in Europe.
choices.textEs: Los programas culturales se justificaban porque el arte y la literatura estadounidenses exportados por la WPA sirvieron como herramientas de poder blando que mejoraron el prestigio estadounidense en el extranjero durante un período de creciente fascismo en Europa.

choices.text: The cultural programs were primarily justified as propaganda tools that allowed the Roosevelt administration to use art and theater to build public support for the New Deal among skeptical middle-class Americans.
choices.textEs: Los programas culturales se justificaban principalmente como herramientas de propaganda que permitían a la administración Roosevelt usar el arte y el teatro para construir apoyo público al New Deal entre los estadounidenses de clase media escépticos.

items.explanation: The WPA cultural programs served multiple functions beyond economic relief: they preserved and documented American history and culture during a time of national crisis (photographers like Dorothea Lange, writers producing state guides, the Federal Theatre bringing drama to communities that had never seen professional theater). They also maintained the skills of trained artists who would otherwise have abandoned their crafts, and they contributed to national morale and cultural identity at a moment of profound despair. The argument goes beyond 'it created jobs' to the question of what a civilization owes its artists and what government's relationship to culture should be. Students must construct and evaluate an argument beyond the literal function of the program.
items.explanationEs: Los programas culturales de la WPA cumplieron múltiples funciones más allá del alivio económico: preservaron y documentaron la historia y la cultura estadounidenses durante una época de crisis nacional (fotógrafos como Dorothea Lange, escritores produciendo guías estatales, el Teatro Federal llevando el drama a comunidades que nunca habían visto teatro profesional). También mantuvieron las habilidades de artistas capacitados que de otro modo habrían abandonado sus oficios, y contribuyeron a la moral nacional y la identidad cultural en un momento de profunda desesperación.

items.stem: The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) was established in 1934 to regulate the stock market. A student argues that the SEC was the New Deal's MOST important long-term institutional legacy. Which reasoning provides the STRONGEST support for this claim?
items.stemEs: La Comisión de Bolsa y Valores (SEC) fue establecida en 1934 para regular el mercado de valores. Un estudiante argumenta que la SEC fue el legado institucional a largo plazo MÁS importante del New Deal. ¿Qué razonamiento proporciona el apoyo MÁS SÓLIDO para esta afirmación?

choices.text: The SEC was the most important legacy because it generated more federal revenue through fines and penalties than any other New Deal regulatory agency, funding subsequent social programs.
choices.textEs: La SEC fue el legado más importante porque generó más ingresos federales a través de multas y penalidades que cualquier otra agencia reguladora del New Deal, financiando programas sociales posteriores.

choices.text: The SEC was the most important legacy because it was the first federal agency to employ large numbers of professional economists and lawyers, establishing the model of expert-driven regulatory governance.
choices.textEs: La SEC fue el legado más importante porque fue la primera agencia federal en emplear a grandes números de economistas y abogados profesionales, estableciendo el modelo de gobernanza regulatoria impulsada por expertos.

choices.text: The SEC established the permanent principle that financial markets require government oversight to prevent the fraud, speculation, and information asymmetry that caused the 1929 collapse — a structural reform that addressed the root causes of the Depression, not just its symptoms.
choices.textEs: La SEC estableció el principio permanente de que los mercados financieros requieren supervisión gubernamental para prevenir el fraude, la especulación y la asimetría de información que causaron el colapso de 1929, una reforma estructural que abordó las causas raíz de la Depresión, no solo sus síntomas.

choices.text: The SEC was the most important legacy because it was the only New Deal agency that survived the Supreme Court's constitutional challenges of 1935–1936 completely intact, demonstrating its broad bipartisan support.
choices.textEs: La SEC fue el legado más importante porque fue la única agencia del New Deal que sobrevivió completamente intacta a los desafíos constitucionales de la Corte Suprema de 1935-1936, demostrando su amplio apoyo bipartidista.

items.explanation: The SEC's long-term institutional significance lies in establishing the principle that financial markets require permanent government oversight to function honestly — a principle that endures today and was dramatically validated by crises like the 2008 financial collapse, when inadequate regulation allowed practices similar to 1920s speculation to reoccur. The SEC addressed the root cause of the financial panic: fraud, information asymmetry, and speculative excess. Social Security addresses citizens' welfare; the FDIC protects deposits; but the SEC addresses the systemic transparency of financial markets themselves, making it a foundational institution for modern capitalism. Students must evaluate competing institutional claims — a DOK 3 task.
items.explanationEs: La importancia institucional a largo plazo de la SEC radica en establecer el principio de que los mercados financieros requieren supervisión gubernamental permanente para funcionar honestamente, un principio que perdura hoy y fue dramáticamente validado por crisis como el colapso financiero de 2008. La SEC abordó la causa raíz del pánico financiero: el fraude, la asimetría de información y el exceso especulativo.

items.stem: The Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 established a national minimum wage and maximum work week. A business owner in 1938 argues the minimum wage will increase unemployment by forcing employers to hire fewer workers. An economist defending the Act argues it will increase employment. Which economic reasoning MOST effectively supports the economist's counter-argument?
items.stemEs: La Ley de Normas Justas de Trabajo de 1938 estableció un salario mínimo nacional y una semana laboral máxima. Un empresario en 1938 argumenta que el salario mínimo aumentará el desempleo al obligar a los empleadores a contratar menos trabajadores. Un economista que defiende la ley argumenta que aumentará el empleo. ¿Qué razonamiento económico apoya MÁS eficazmente el contraargumento del economista?

choices.text: A minimum wage prevents employers from engaging in wage competition that drives wages to unsustainable levels, protecting the entire labor market from a race to the bottom that ultimately destroys purchasing power.
choices.textEs: Un salario mínimo impide que los empleadores participen en una competencia salarial que lleva los salarios a niveles insostenibles, protegiendo a todo el mercado laboral de una carrera hacia el fondo que en última instancia destruye el poder adquisitivo.

choices.text: By reducing the maximum work week to 40 hours, the Act forces employers to hire additional workers to cover the same number of total work hours, directly increasing employment without any cost per employee.
choices.textEs: Al reducir la semana laboral máxima a 40 horas, la ley obliga a los empleadores a contratar trabajadores adicionales para cubrir el mismo número total de horas de trabajo, aumentando directamente el empleo sin ningún costo por empleado.

choices.text: In a demand-starved economy, raising wages for low-income workers who spend most of their income directly increases consumer demand for goods, which increases production and creates more jobs than the labor cost increases eliminate.
choices.textEs: En una economía hambrienta de demanda, aumentar los salarios de los trabajadores de bajos ingresos que gastan la mayor parte de sus ingresos aumenta directamente la demanda del consumidor de bienes, lo que aumenta la producción y crea más empleos de los que eliminan los aumentos de costos laborales.

choices.text: The minimum wage applies equally to all employers, so no individual business is disadvantaged competitively by paying higher wages, eliminating the employer's incentive to respond to higher labor costs by cutting employment.
choices.textEs: El salario mínimo se aplica por igual a todos los empleadores, por lo que ninguna empresa individual está en desventaja competitiva por pagar salarios más altos, eliminando el incentivo del empleador para responder a los mayores costos laborales reduciendo el empleo.

items.explanation: The demand-side argument for minimum wages in a depressed economy is: when wages are too low, workers cannot afford to buy goods; when workers cannot buy goods, businesses cannot sell products; when businesses cannot sell, they lay off more workers, deepening the depression. Raising the minimum wage increases the purchasing power of the workers most likely to spend it (low-income workers who spend nearly all marginal income), which creates demand for goods, which increases production and hiring. This is the Keynesian demand-side counter-argument to the supply-side (labor cost) argument. Students must reason through competing economic frameworks at DOK 3.
items.explanationEs: El argumento del lado de la demanda para los salarios mínimos en una economía deprimida es: cuando los salarios son demasiado bajos, los trabajadores no pueden permitirse comprar bienes; cuando los trabajadores no pueden comprar bienes, las empresas no pueden vender productos; cuando las empresas no pueden vender, despiden a más trabajadores, profundizando la depresión. Aumentar el salario mínimo incrementa el poder adquisitivo de los trabajadores con más probabilidades de gastarlo (trabajadores de bajos ingresos que gastan casi todo el ingreso marginal), lo que crea demanda de bienes, lo que aumenta la producción y la contratación.

items.stem: Historian Christopher Browning's research on German Reserve Police Battalion 101 found that ordinary middle-aged men — not committed ideological Nazis — committed mass executions of Jewish civilians after being explicitly offered the option to refuse without penalty. What does this evidence suggest about the primary mechanisms enabling mass atrocity?

choices.text: The Holocaust's perpetration relied not solely on fanatical ideologues but on ordinary people responding to situational pressures — obedience to authority, conformity to group behavior, and gradual moral habituation to violence — revealing that genocide requires participation of ordinary individuals operating within systems that normalize extraordinary atrocity.

Browning's findings establish that the German people as a whole bore collective moral and legal responsibility for the Holocaust, since ordinary citizens who were not ideologically committed to Nazism nevertheless chose active participation in mass murder when given explicit freedom to refuse.

The willingness of non-ideological Germans to carry out executions confirms Daniel Goldhagen's 'eliminationist antisemitism' thesis, which holds that a culturally distinctive German antisemitic worldview rather than situational pressures was the principal explanatory factor in Holocaust perpetration.

The Battalion 101 evidence suggests that military hierarchy and command obedience were the decisive enabling mechanisms, since the men killed primarily because they had been conditioned through training to follow orders rather than exercise independent moral judgment in field conditions.

items.explanation: Browning's Battalion 101 study is foundational evidence in the perpetrator motivation debate because the men were not selected for their antisemitic enthusiasm or military conditioning — making situational factors such as conformity, deference to authority, and gradual psychological desensitization rather than ideological commitment the most supported explanation for their participation.

items.stem: When the MS St. Louis carrying 937 Jewish refugees was refused entry by Cuba, the United States, and Canada in 1939, President Roosevelt declined to use available executive authority to admit the passengers. How should historians evaluate American refugee policy in light of developing knowledge about Nazi persecution of Jews?

choices.text: American refugee policy reflected the practical political constraints of economic depression and high domestic unemployment, suggesting the refusal to admit Jewish refugees was an understandable response to domestic conditions rather than evidence of indifference to antisemitic persecution.

The Roosevelt administration's refusal to act despite documented knowledge of Nazi persecution and available executive options represents a failure of moral and political leadership that cannot be fully explained by domestic political constraints alone — revealing that antisemitic attitudes within the State Department and fear of political backlash both played significant roles in shaping refugee policy.

U.S. refugee policy was primarily constrained by existing congressional immigration quota laws over which the executive branch had limited independent authority, making specific criticism of Roosevelt for the St. Louis decision historically unfair since the statutory framework left him with minimal options.

The United States' failure to accept Jewish refugees was consistent with the broader Allied pattern of prioritizing military strategy over rescue, demonstrating that all major Allied powers shared equivalent moral responsibility for preventable deaths of refugees who were denied haven before and during the Holocaust.

items.explanation: The combination of State Department obstruction, documented failure to fill available immigration quota slots, and the passive response to the St. Louis when executive options existed creates an evidentiary basis for evaluating the failure as going beyond statutory constraint — representing choices made in an environment where antisemitic bureaucratic attitudes and political calculation shaped policy outcomes.

items.stem: The Nuremberg Trials (1945-46) established that individuals could be held criminally responsible for 'crimes against humanity' and 'crimes against peace' under international law even when acting in an official government capacity. What was the most significant long-term legal implication of this precedent for international order?

choices.text: The Nuremberg principles created an immediately binding body of international criminal law that constrained the behavior of all signatory nations, effectively ending state-sponsored mass atrocity as a recurrent feature of international relations in the postwar decades.

By establishing that 'following orders' was not an absolute defense against criminal liability for atrocities, Nuremberg permanently resolved the philosophical debate over whether soldiers have a moral obligation to refuse clearly unethical commands from superior officers.

The Nuremberg precedent established that state sovereignty does not provide immunity from accountability for mass atrocities, creating the legal foundation for subsequent developments including the Genocide Convention, the International Criminal Court, and the emerging Responsibility to Protect doctrine.

The Nuremberg Trials were primarily instruments of victor's justice rather than genuine international law, and their true legacy was establishing a hypocritical legal standard that victorious powers could apply to defeated enemies while exempting themselves from equivalent accountability for wartime conduct.

items.explanation: Nuremberg's most consequential legal contribution was establishing that governmental authority cannot immunize individuals from criminal responsibility for atrocity — a principle codified in the Genocide Convention (1948), the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (1948), and the ICC Rome Statute (1998), making it the foundational precedent of modern international humanitarian law.

items.stem: The United States Holocaust Memorial Museum adopted 'Remember the Past; Shape the Future' as its institutional mission. A critic argues that Holocaust memory in American public culture has become detached from its specific historical context and transformed into a generalized moral lesson applicable to any political conflict. Which response best evaluates both the value and the risk of universalizing Holocaust memory in this way?

choices.text: Universal application of Holocaust memory is entirely appropriate because genocide is the ultimate human rights violation, and any educational or rhetorical strategy that makes atrocity prevention more likely is justified by its outcomes, regardless of whether historical analogies are precisely calibrated to specific contexts.

Holocaust memory should remain strictly confined to its specific historical, political, and social circumstances because universalization risks antisemitic harm by implying that the Jewish experience of genocide is only meaningful when repurposed as a lesson for non-Jewish political goals and contemporary conflicts.

The 'Never Again' framework has proven empirically effective at building political will for genocide prevention when invoked by powerful nations with military and diplomatic capacity to intervene, making universalization both ethically sound and practically valuable despite its contextual imprecision.

Universalizing Holocaust memory creates genuine value by making genocide's warning signs legible across different historical contexts, but it also creates risk of historical distortion and competitive victimhood when the Holocaust becomes a rhetorical trump card rather than a specifically studied historical event — suggesting that effective Holocaust education must balance universal lessons with rigorous historical particularity.

items.explanation: The most analytically complete evaluation acknowledges genuine pedagogical value in universal lessons drawn from the Holocaust — increasing recognition of warning signs like dehumanization and scapegoating — while also engaging honestly with the risks that imprecise universalization creates: inaccurate analogies, dilution of specific context, and rhetorical abuse that substitutes dramatic comparison for careful historical analysis.

items.stem: The Holocaust was not widely taught in American public schools until the 1970s and 1980s, and Congress did not establish the United States Holocaust Memorial Museum until 1980. What combination of factors best explains the three-decade delay between the end of World War II and the emergence of sustained Holocaust education and commemoration in American public culture?

choices.text: Americans were primarily preoccupied with postwar prosperity and Cold War security anxieties in ways that made the genocide of European Jews a secondary concern, demonstrating that democratic publics require direct political relevance before engaging substantively with atrocities committed against foreign civilians.

Cold War political pressures to normalize relations with West Germany, the initial postwar impulse toward forward-looking optimism over traumatic reckoning, survivor reluctance to testify publicly, and the marginalization of Jewish American voices in mainstream media combined to suppress Holocaust memory until the Eichmann trial, the Six-Day War, and the 1978 NBC Holocaust miniseries created the cultural and political

The U.S. government actively suppressed Holocaust documentation and survivor testimony throughout the 1940s and 1950s because fully acknowledging the genocide would have damaged diplomatic relations with West Germany, a critical NATO ally — making deliberate political calculation rather than cultural inattention the primary cause of delayed commemoration.

The delay reflected the general failure of American educational institutions to incorporate non-American history into curricula during the postwar decades, as nationalist historiographical frameworks across Western educational systems prevented systematic engagement with international atrocities in standard course offerings.

items.explanation: Holocaust memory's delayed emergence resulted from multiple converging factors: Cold War imperatives toward West German normalization, the psychological difficulty of survivor testimony, institutional barriers Jewish Americans faced in mainstream media, and the absence of a sustained commemoration infrastructure — until specific historical events created the political and emotional conditions for public engagement. items.stem:
Use the photograph to answer the question.

This photograph shows FDR delivering a fireside chat.

(Photograph, c. 1933. Public Domain.)

Analyze how Roosevelt's communication strategies, including the fireside chats, helped him build support for the expansion of federal power during the New Deal.
items.stemEs: Analice cómo las estrategias de comunicación de Roosevelt le ayudaron a construir apoyo para la expansión del poder federal.

choices.text: By explaining complex policies in accessible language and framing government action as necessary to protect ordinary Americans, Roosevelt built public trust that sustained support for unprecedented federal programs
Roosevelt's fireside chats failed to generate support, and New Deal programs were passed only because Congress acted independently
The fireside chats were used exclusively to criticize the Supreme Court and had no connection to New Deal legislation
Roosevelt avoided discussing specific policies in his radio addresses to prevent public opposition

items.explanation: FDR's communication genius lay in making the expansion of federal power feel necessary and personal. His first fireside chat explained the banking crisis so clearly that deposits returned to banks the next day. By framing programs like Social Security and the TVA as protecting 'the forgotten man,' he built a political coalition that sustained the New Deal despite fierce opposition from business leaders and the Supreme Court.
items.explanationEs: Roosevelt hizo que la expansión del poder federal se sintiera necesaria y personal, construyendo una coalición política que sostuvo el New Deal.

items.stem:
Use the photograph to answer the question.

This iconic photograph, known as 'Migrant Mother,' was taken by Dorothea Lange in 1936 in Nipomo, California. It shows Florence Owens Thompson, a 32-year-old mother of seven, with a deeply worried expression, her hand touching her face. Two of her children lean against her shoulders with their faces turned away from the camera. The photograph was taken to document conditions facing migrant farmworkers during the Great Depression.

(Photograph by Dorothea Lange, 1936. Library of Congress, Farm Security Administration/Office of War Information Collection.)

Evaluate how FSA photography like 'Migrant Mother' served as both documentary evidence and government propaganda in support of New Deal programs.

choices.text: FSA photographs documented genuine hardship while also being deliberately framed to build emotional public support for government relief programs, serving both documentary and persuasive purposes
FSA photographs were entirely staged propaganda with no connection to actual conditions faced by migrant workers
FSA photographs were purely objective documents with no intention of influencing public opinion or government policy
FSA photographs had little public impact because they were only seen by government officials and were never widely distributed

items.explanation: FSA photographs genuinely documented real conditions of poverty and hardship — in that sense they were authentic documentary evidence. At the same time, photographers were guided by FSA administrators to select subjects and compositions that would build emotional support for New Deal relief programs, making the images serve a persuasive government purpose. This dual function distinguishes FSA photography from purely neutral documentary work. Choice B overstates the propaganda dimension by denying their documentary value. Choice C ignores the intentional rhetorical framing. Choice D is factually incorrect — the FSA photography project was widely distributed and had significant public impact.

items.stem: Critics of the New Deal from the left, including Huey Long and socialist intellectuals, argued it preserved capitalism without genuine structural transformation, while critics from the right argued it represented dangerous federal overreach. What does the existence of this two-sided criticism most reveal about the New Deal's actual ideological character and historical significance?

choices.text: The New Deal occupied a reform-without-revolution position — it stabilized the capitalist system by addressing its most destabilizing failures without fundamentally redistributing wealth or restructuring ownership — making it an ideologically moderate but historically unprecedented response to economic catastrophe that satisfied neither ideological extreme.

Roosevelt's political genius lay in synthesizing elements of both left and right criticism into a coherent program, borrowing regulatory ideas from progressives and efficiency principles from business conservatives to create pragmatic policies that maintained political viability by satisfying neither extreme.

The two-sided criticism demonstrates that the New Deal was an incoherent collection of experimental programs lacking a unifying reform philosophy, which is why historians continue to debate whether it extended or shortened the Depression's duration rather than agreeing on a definitive assessment.

The New Deal's primary significance was its expansion of the permanent federal bureaucratic apparatus and the precedent it established for government economic intervention, regardless of whether its specific programs effectively accelerated economic recovery from the Depression.

items.explanation: The fact that Long attacked the New Deal for not going far enough while business conservatives attacked it for going too far locates it precisely in the ideologically moderate reform space: it used federal power to manage capitalism's most destructive tendencies without threatening the fundamental structures of private ownership and profit that left critics demanded be dismantled. items.explanation: B is correct: The New Deal fundamentally transformed the relationship between the federal government and citizens by establishing the principle that the government had a responsibility to provide economic security — through Social Security, unemployment insurance, bank deposit guarantees, and labor protections. Programs like the FDIC and Social Security persisted long after the Depression and reshaped expectations of government's role in citizens' lives. A is incorrect: the New Deal expanded federal power significantly; it did not restore pre-Depression limited government. C is incorrect: the New Deal did not succeed in fully ending the Depression — World War II mobilization did more to restore full employment. D is incorrect: the New Deal focused on domestic economic recovery, not foreign policy or international institutions.

Extended Response: Economic Policy from the New Deal to the Great Recession

Using your knowledge of U.S. History from the New Deal era through the 2008 financial crisis, write an extended response that constructs a fully developed, evidence-based argument addressing the following question:

How did the deregulatory economic philosophy of the Reagan Revolution (US.83) create the conditions for the 2008 financial crisis (US.93), and what does this arc reveal about the recurring tension in American political economy between market freedom and government regulation?

Your response must: (1) state a clear, historically defensible thesis connecting Reagan-era deregulation to the 2008 financial crisis; (2) provide at least three specific pieces of historical evidence tracing this policy arc from the 1980s through 2008; (3) demonstrate cross-era synthesis by connecting this arc to the regulatory response to the Great Depression (US.39–US.44) that Reagan-era deregulation was dismantling; and (4) evaluate whether the post-2008 regulatory response (Dodd-Frank) represented a return to New Deal-style regulation or a fundamentally different approach.
items.stemEs:
Respuesta Extendida: Política Económica desde el New Deal hasta la Gran Recesión

Usando su conocimiento de la Historia de EE. UU. desde la era del New Deal hasta la crisis financiera de 2008, escriba una respuesta extendida que construya un argumento completamente desarrollado y basado en evidencia abordando la siguiente pregunta:

¿Cómo la filosofía económica desregulatoria de la Revolución Reagan (US.83) creó las condiciones para la crisis financiera de 2008 (US.93), y qué revela este arco sobre la tensión recurrente en la economía política estadounidense entre la libertad de mercado y la regulación gubernamental?

Su respuesta debe: (1) plantear una tesis clara y históricamente defendible que conecte la desregulación de la era Reagan con la crisis financiera de 2008; (2) proporcionar al menos tres piezas específicas de evidencia histórica trazando este arco de política desde los años 80 hasta 2008; (3) demostrar síntesis entre eras conectando este arco con la respuesta regulatoria a la Gran Depresión (US.39–US.44) que la desregulación de la era Reagan estaba desmantelando; y (4) evaluar si la respuesta regulatoria posterior a 2008 (Dodd-Frank) representó un retorno a la regulación al estilo del New Deal o un enfoque fundamentalmente diferente.
items.correctAnswer: A top-score response argues that Reagan-era deregulation created a 25-year policy arc that progressively dismantled the regulatory architecture built after the 1929 crash, creating the specific conditions — deregulated financial instruments, removed firewall between commercial and investment banking, unregulated derivatives — that enabled the 2008 crisis. Thesis: The 2008 financial crisis was not a random market failure but the predictable, delayed consequence of the deliberate dismantling of Depression-era financial regulation, demonstrating that the recurring cycle of deregulation-crisis-re-regulation is a structural feature of American capitalism that no single regulatory settlement permanently resolves. Evidence tracing the arc: (1) Reagan-era S&L deregulation (Garn-St. Germain Act, 1982) removed interest-rate ceilings and expanded S&L investment authority — producing the Savings and Loan Crisis of the late 1980s, a $132 billion bailout that was a direct preview of 2008; (2) the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act (1999, Clinton) repealed Glass-Steagall (1933), allowing commercial banks to enter investment banking — the enabling condition for mortgage-backed securities and CDO creation; (3) the Commodity Futures Modernization Act (2000) deregulated the derivatives market, allowing credit default swaps to grow to $60+ trillion — the specific mechanism of AIG's near-collapse in 2008. Cross-era synthesis with New Deal regulation: The Glass-Steagall Act (1933) and the Securities Exchange Act (1934) were enacted precisely because the 1920s deregulated financial speculation had produced the 1929 crash and Great Depression. Reagan-era deregulators argued that Depression-era regulation was overcautious and economically inefficient — and spent 25 years proving their predecessors' caution correct. Evaluation of Dodd-Frank: The Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act (2010) represented a different regulatory approach than the New Deal — rather than structural separation (Glass-Steagall), it imposed stress testing, resolution authority, the Volcker Rule (limiting proprietary trading), and the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau — a more technocratic, regulatory approach than structural prohibition. Whether Dodd-Frank was sufficient became contested when the Trump administration partially rolled it back (2018 Economic Growth Act), suggesting the deregulation cycle was beginning again.
